lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Yes, But
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Henrique Monteiro Neto | Lesson 7 -- Yes, But

listenings.text: A brief note on how this was actually introduced, because the sequence matters. It was rolled out in four regions first, deliberately chosen to be different from one another, and it ran there for eighteen months before anybody committed to going further. It is now being phased in nationally over six years, which is a long time, and I would say frankly that six years is a political number rather than an economic one. Two things happened that were not in the plan. An unintended consequence appeared in the rental market inside the first year, and it took another year to measure properly. And for the very largest firms the first stage produced a windfall, most of which the treasury clawed back through the tax code, though not all of it, and not quickly.

Let me start with what I accept, because I think my colleagues on this side skip it too quickly. Waiting times fell. That is real, it is measured, and it is not a rounding error. Granted also that the scheme was introduced carefully, in four regions, and that whoever designed the sequence knew what they were doing. And I accept that the alternative under discussion at the time was in some respects worse. That said, my objection stands, and it is this. It is a blunt instrument. A targeted scheme would have achieved most of the same result for considerably less money, and the reason we did not build one is that targeting is administratively hard and politically thankless. I am not arguing that anybody acted in bad faith. I am arguing that we chose the easy design and then congratulated ourselves on the outcome.

extra_audio.text: Alice says people assume that because she defends the scheme she thinks it is perfect. He asks her to start with the strongest objection rather than the easiest one. She concedes that the scheme is regressive at the bottom of the scale. She explains that the rebate offsets most of it, though not all, and that the alternative was worse. She says she would vote for it with reservations, and would not design it that way again.
